ad-flank-attack|vlakte.reden: Flank Attack — setup 1 of 7 this Act, the setups are dealt out across the Act, so no two battles play alike. The attacker holds back a flanking force of up to ⅓ of their points, and the defender guards the Baggage Train in their own zone.
ad-flank-attack|vlakte.blurb: The attacker splits their army and comes in from the side, while the defender guards the baggage.
ad-flank-attack|vlakte.deployNote: Defender along the top edge, attacker along the bottom: zones 12″ deep, at least 24″ apart and 12″ clear of the side edges. Before deployment the attacker sets aside a flanking force of up to ⅓ of their points (whole units only) and nominates the left or right edge — the blue strip shows that edge in the defender's half; mirror it for the other side. The defender places the Baggage Train (60×100 mm) wholly inside their own deployment zone, at least 3″ from every table edge, not in terrain and not on a low wall. Deploy alternately, one unit at a time (the winner of a roll-off chooses who deploys the first unit). Once deployment is complete, roll off: the winner takes the first turn, and the player who finished deploying their army first adds +1 to the roll.
ad-flank-attack|vlakte.gameEnd: Six turns, decided on Victory Points. From the attacker's third turn, roll a D6 at the start of each of their turns for the flanking force: it arrives on a 4+ in turn 3, a 3+ in turn 4 and a 2+ from turn 5, along the nominated edge in the defender's half. It may march, but not charge, on the turn it arrives. Its units do not have to arrive together: any left off the table may move on in a later Movement phase. The Baggage Train is controlled by a unit with Unit Strength 10 or more within 6″ that is not fleeing and has not succumbed to Stupidity; the closest one controls it, and if two enemy units are equally close it is contested. To destroy it, an attacking unit with Unit Strength 5 or more moves into base contact in the Remaining Moves sub-phase; while in contact it cannot shoot and may only cast spells with a range of Combat or Self. If at the start of its next turn it is still in contact, still has Unit Strength 5 or more, and is not in combat and not fleeing, the Baggage Train is destroyed and removed. If the defender controls the Baggage Train at the end, they score 120 VP; if the attacker destroys it, the attacker scores 300 VP.

posten.label: Flank Attack: Baggage Train held at the end
posten.uitleg: The defender controls the Baggage Train at the end (the closest unit with Unit Strength 10+ within 6″ that is not fleeing and has not succumbed to Stupidity; two enemy units equally close = contested).

posten.label: Flank Attack: Baggage Train destroyed
posten.uitleg: An attacking unit (Unit Strength 5+) moved into base contact in the Remaining Moves sub-phase and at the start of its next turn was still in contact, still Unit Strength 5+, not in combat and not fleeing.

ad-breakthrough|vlakte.reden: Breakthrough — setup 1 of 7 this Act, the setups are dealt out across the Act, so no two battles play alike. On top of normal Victory Points, the attacker scores every unit that ends wholly inside the defender's deployment zone.
ad-breakthrough|vlakte.blurb: The attacker must smash through the line and reach the ground behind it.
ad-breakthrough|vlakte.deployNote: Zones 12″ deep, at least 24″ apart and 12″ clear of the side edges. The defender has a low wall and places it in their own half before deployment. The attacker deploys their whole army first, then the defender deploys their whole army. The defender takes the first turn.
ad-breakthrough|vlakte.gameEnd: Six turns, decided on Victory Points; both sides score Victory Points as normal. On top of that, at the end the attacker scores the points value of every attacking unit wholly inside the defender's deployment zone (not fleeing units, monsters or characters).

posten.label: Breakthrough: units in the defender’s zone
posten.uitleg: At the end: the points value of every attacking unit wholly inside the defender’s deployment zone (not fleeing units, monsters or characters).

ad-command-control|vlakte.reden: Command & Control — setup 1 of 7 this Act, the setups are dealt out across the Act, so no two battles play alike. A special feature stands dead centre: control it for a random bonus each turn and Victory Points at the end.
ad-command-control|vlakte.blurb: A special feature in the middle of the field decides it — neither side can ignore the centre.
ad-command-control|vlakte.deployNote: Standard 12″ zones. A special feature (★, no more than 6″ wide, impassable, no line of sight through it) stands dead centre and does not scatter. Deploy alternately, one unit at a time (the winner of a roll-off chooses who deploys the first unit). Once deployment is complete, roll off: the winner takes the first turn, and the player who finished deploying their army first adds +1 to the roll.
ad-command-control|vlakte.gameEnd: Six turns, decided on Victory Points. The feature is controlled by proximity only: by a unit with Unit Strength 5 or more within 6″ that is not fleeing. If more than one eligible unit is within 6″, the closest one controls it; if two enemy units are equally close, it is contested and neither controls it. In every Start of Turn in which you control it, roll a D6 for the controlling unit, until the end of that turn: 1-2 Magic Resistance (-3), 3-4 Hatred (all enemies), 5-6 Unbreakable. At the end of each player's turn, the side that controls it scores 10 VP; after your own turn and after your opponent's, so one side can score up to 12 times. Controlling it at the end of the battle scores a further 200 VP.

posten.label: Command & Control: special feature held at the end of a player’s turn
posten.uitleg: At the end of each player’s turn, the side that controls the special feature scores this (proximity only: the closest unit with Unit Strength 5+ within 6″ that is not fleeing; two enemy units equally close = contested): after your own turn and after your opponent’s, so one side can score up to 12 times.

posten.label: Command & Control: special feature held at the end
posten.uitleg: Whoever controls the special feature at the end of the battle (proximity only: the closest unit with Unit Strength 5+ within 6″ that is not fleeing; two enemy units equally close = contested).

ad-strategic|vlakte.reden: Strategic Locations — setup 1 of 7 this Act, the setups are dealt out across the Act, so no two battles play alike. Three markers beyond the defender's zone: the defender holds them, the attacker destroys them.
ad-strategic|vlakte.blurb: Three positions on the defender's ground. The defender holds them; the attacker comes to wreck them.
ad-strategic|vlakte.deployNote: Standard 12″ zones. Three objective markers stand 4″ beyond the defender's deployment zone, at a quarter, half and three quarters of the table width; a marker is never within 3″ of terrain or on a low wall. Deploy alternately, one unit at a time (the winner of a roll-off chooses who deploys the first unit). Once deployment is complete, roll off: the winner takes the first turn, and the player who finished deploying their army first adds +1 to the roll.
ad-strategic|vlakte.gameEnd: Six turns, decided on Victory Points. The defender holds a marker with a Core unit with Unit Strength 10 or more within 6″ that is not fleeing and has not succumbed to Stupidity; the closest one controls it (equal distance: the higher Unit Strength; still equal: contested). The attacker cannot hold them, only destroy them: an attacking unit with Unit Strength 5 or more moves into base contact in the Remaining Moves sub-phase; while in contact it cannot shoot and may only cast spells with a range of Combat or Self. If at the start of its next turn it is still in contact, still has Unit Strength 5 or more, and is not in combat and not fleeing, the marker is destroyed and removed. The defender scores 60 VP for every marker still standing that they control at the end; the attacker scores 100 VP for every marker destroyed.

posten.label: Strategic Locations: marker standing and held at the end
posten.uitleg: Per marker still standing that the defender controls at the end (the closest Core unit with Unit Strength 10+ within 6″ that is not fleeing and has not succumbed to Stupidity).

posten.label: Strategic Locations: marker destroyed
posten.uitleg: Per marker the attacker destroyed. A destroyed marker cannot also be held: the two together are never more than 3.

ad-loot-cart|vlakte.reden: Plunder — setup 1 of 7 this Act, the setups are dealt out across the Act, so no two battles play alike. Two storage buildings in the defender's zone: the attacker plunders them for Victory Points, turn after turn.
ad-loot-cart|vlakte.blurb: Two storage buildings behind the defender's line, and a raiding force that wants what is inside.
ad-loot-cart|vlakte.deployNote: Attacker: 12″ deep along the whole bottom edge. Defender: 12″ deep at the top, starting 11″ in from each side (16″ on a 72″ table). Two storage buildings (impassable, no more than 6″) stand in the front corners of the defender's zone. The defender deploys first, alternating units, and takes the first turn.
ad-loot-cart|vlakte.gameEnd: Six turns, decided on Victory Points. At the end of each attacker's turn, every storage building with an attacking unit in base contact (Unit Strength 5 or more, not in combat, not fleeing, not succumbed to Stupidity) is plundered — once per storage building per turn; the storage buildings stay. The attacker scores 25 VP per plunder. The defender starts with a pot of 100 VP and loses 10 VP of it per plunder, down to 0.

posten.label: Plunder: storage building plundered
posten.uitleg: Per plunder: at the end of each attacker’s turn, once per storage building, with an attacking unit (Unit Strength 5+) in base contact, not in combat, not fleeing and not succumbed to Stupidity. No cap.

posten.label: Plunder: what is left of the defender’s pot
posten.uitleg: The defender starts with this pot and loses part of it for every plunder, down to 0; what is left is theirs at the end.

ad-special-feature|vlakte.reden: The Forge — setup 1 of 7 this Act, the setups are dealt out across the Act, so no two battles play alike. The Forge stands at the edge of the defender's corner: the defender scores every turn they hold it, the attacker deploys last and moves first.
ad-special-feature|vlakte.blurb: One building worth fighting over: whoever holds it arms themselves from it.
ad-special-feature|vlakte.deployNote: Deployment zones are quarter circles in opposite corners: 24″ on a 48×48 table, 30″ on 72×48 (defender top right, attacker bottom left). The defender deploys their whole army first, then the attacker deploys their whole army. The attacker takes the first turn. The Forge (impassable, no more than 6″) stands on the diagonal at the edge of the defender's zone.
ad-special-feature|vlakte.gameEnd: Six turns, decided on Victory Points. The Forge is controlled by a unit with Unit Strength 5 or more within 3″ that is not fleeing and has not succumbed to Stupidity; the closest one controls it (equal distance: the higher Unit Strength; still equal: contested). The controlling unit gains Armour Bane (1) and loses it as soon as it stops controlling the Forge. At the end of each player's turn in which the defender controls the Forge, the defender scores 25 VP. The attacker does not score for it: taking the Forge stops the defender scoring and arms the attacker's unit.

posten.label: The Forge: held at the end of a player’s turn
posten.uitleg: At the end of each player’s turn (both players’ turns count, so at most 12) in which the defender controls the Forge (the closest unit with Unit Strength 5+ within 3″ that is not fleeing and has not succumbed to Stupidity).
